## Diagram Description

The signal-to-action flow diagram is the canonical technical architecture visualization. It shows how raw signals from any domain become governed, audited actions through the Lyte + Alloy spine.

### Flow Steps

```
Signals → Normalization → Context Engine (Lyte) → Routing Engine (Alloy)
                                                          │
                                          ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                                          ▼               ▼               ▼
                                    Auto-Execute    Approval Gate    Human Review
                                          │               │               │
                                          └───────────────┼───────────────┘
                                                          ▼
                                                   Action Execution
                                                          │
                                                          ▼
                                                Immutable Audit Trail
```

### Step Details

| Step | System | Key Functions |
|------|--------|---------------|
| Signals | Domain-specific | People drift, revenue stall, infra anomaly, security event, market shift |
| Normalization | Alloy | Schema validation, source tagging, dedup & merge, priority scoring |
| Context Engine | Lyte | PRISM correlation, AI inference, evidence packaging, confidence scoring |
| Routing Engine | Alloy | Policy evaluation, approval matrix, escalation rules, cost controls |
| Auto-Execute | Alloy | Low-risk, policy-approved, immediate action |
| Approval Gate | Alloy + Human | Medium risk, human-in-the-loop |
| Human Review | Human | High-risk, analyst required |
| Action Execution | Platform | Webhook, API, notification, workflow trigger |
| Audit Trail | Platform | Append-only, actor, timestamp, evidence |

### Domain Pack Note

The diagram includes a callout showing that Aegis, Vessels, and Terra each apply this same architecture to their vertical signal sources (security events, AIS fleet data, real estate distress signals).
